incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENCE ALERT: Spike of 500s on /v1/embeddings (region: eu-west1) — auto-fallbacks observed to chat variants. Paging oncall.

maria_liu: seeing this since 12:03 UTC. error rate ~18% on embeddings route. traces show requests routed to model variant 'redwood-chat-v2' even though alias pinned to 'embed-quantized-v1'.

alex_kapoor: confirmed. sample from logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:04:12Z GET /v1/embeddings?model=embed-quantized-v1 -> 200 (but body type: chat)
request_id=abc123
input=["invoice 1234 ..."]
response_type=chat
```

samir_ng: that explains 415/422 client validation failures at downstream embedding consumers. Chat payload doesn't match embedding schema.

maria_liu: initial hypothesis: routing fallback policy on alias fallback_map allowed chat-compatible variant when reserved model not available. But embed->chat is semantically incompatible.

eng-runtime: (bot) routing policy event: alias "enterprise-ingest" resolved to anchor "embed-quantized-v1" but runtime selected candidate "redwood-chat-v2-compat" due to capacity & pin mismatch. Fallback policy = "loose_variant_compatibility".

alex_kapoor: we need an immediate mitigator: disable cross-interface fallback for alias enterprise-ingest in eu-west1 and quarantine pinned version.

maria_liu: I'm going to add a temporary rule to route to the next compatible embedding variant only (no chat/instruct). Doing now.

ops-bot: permission-check OK. Applying routing override: {
  "alias": "enterprise-ingest",
  "region": "eu-west1",
  "allow_cross_interface_fallback": false,
  "override_id": "temp-2612345678"
}

maria_liu: override applied. Monitoring.

jordan_w: customer impact? Which tenants affected?

maria_liu: preliminary: ~4% of total embeddings traffic, concentrated on two large tenants (Acme Payments, NovaML). Acme reported malformed embeddings downstream (metrics alert). Escalating to account team.

samir_ng: starting a canary rollback of anchor pin to previous stable variant (embed-quantized-v0.9) for eu-west1.

eng-runtime: (bot) rollback job started: rollback_id=rb-2612345678, target_variant=embed-quantized-v0.9, expected completion ~2m.

alex_kapoor: If rollback fails, plan B is to disable alias entirely for write path and return 503 with clear error so clients can backoff.

maria_liu: rollback succeeded at 12:09 UTC. Error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.5% in the next 30s. Still seeing a handful of old routed requests for ~60s TTL.

jordan_w: good. Can you confirm no user data was exposed? Any PII leakage because of model switch?

maria_liu: no signs of content transform leaking -- this is strictly interface mismatch (chat object vs vector). We'll run a small search for chat tokens in embedding logs.

ops-bot: audit: routing decisions for alias enterprise-ingest between 12:00-12:10 UTC: 472k requests, 18k routed to chat variant.

samir_ng: notifying sales/CS for impacted customers. @jordan_w can you lead the customer comms? recommend status: "partial degradation, embeddings temporarily inconsistent; mitigation applied".

jordan_w: on it. Draft: "We're investigating a routing bug that caused some embedding requests to be handled by a chat variant. We've reverted the routing and are validating outputs. No customer data was exposed." Will post in #customer-status.

alex_kapoor: postmortem owner? Suggest engineering-assigned: @maria_liu, runtime lead for root cause: fallback policy allowed cross-interface mapping when anchor mismatch and capacity low. We'll need stricter compatibility checks at routing layer and a test harness to simulate variant-starvation.

maria_liu: taking postmortem. Action items I already noted:
- tighten fallback policy enum (no cross-interface fallbacks by default)
- add invariant checks to routing: require model_interface == requested_interface
- add e2e test for pinned anchor missing -> ensure fallback selection respects interface
- alert rule on routing anomalies (sudden cross-interface % > 0.5%)

samir_ng: handing off to night oncall @samir_ng for watch. I'll add runbook notes.

samir_ng: ack. I’ll monitor for next 4 hours and escalate if >1% error reappears. tagging incident as sev2. :white_check_mark:
